paragraphs.text: “It,” masc., referring to the “cloud mass,” masc.
“It,” fem., evidently referring to the “fire,” fem.
Lit., “the electrum.” Heb., ha·chash·malʹ; Gr., e·lekʹtrou; Lat., e·lecʹtri. A shining alloy of gold and silver.
Lit., “like the eye of.” Heb., keʽehnʹ.
“The spirit.” Heb., ha·ruʹach; Gr., pneuʹma; Lat., spiʹri·tus. Compare vs 4 ftn, “Wind.”
“The living creatures.” Heb., ha·chai·yohthʹ, fem. pl.; Gr., zoiʹon, the same word as in Re 4:6-9; Lat., a·ni·maʹli·um.
Possibly, centered at right angles on the same axis.
“Son of man.” Heb., ben-ʼa·dhamʹ; the first of 93 occurrences of this expression in Ezekiel. Gr., hui·eʹ an·throʹpou; Lat., fiʹli hoʹmi·nis.

“The Sovereign Lord Jehovah.” Heb., ʼAdho·naiʹ Yeho·wihʹ, with ʼAdho·naiʹ pl. to denote excellence, hence rendered “Sovereign Lord”; T, “Jehovah God”; Sy, “the Lord of lords”; Lat., Doʹmi·nus Deʹus; Luther (German, 1912 ed.), der Herr HErr, “the Lord LORD (Jehovah).” The first occurrence of this expression is in Ge 15:2, and it appears 217 times in Ezekiel. See App 1E.
“A spirit.” Heb., ruʹach; Gr., pneuʹma; Lat., spiʹri·tus. Compare 1:4 ftn, “Wind.”
“And I began to dwell,” Mmargin and many Heb. mss.
“You will positively die.” Lit., “Dying you [sing.] will die.” Heb., mohth ta·muthʹ. See Ge 2:17 ftn.
“Your own soul.” Heb., naph·shekhaʹ; Gr., psy·khenʹ sou; Lat., aʹni·mam tuʹam. See App 4A.
“A man.” Heb., leʼishʹ; Gr., anʹdra; Lat., vir.
“To the wind.” Heb., la·ruʹach; Gr., pneuʹma·ti; Lat., venʹtum. Compare Ge 1:2 ftn, “Force.”
“You,” fem. sing., referring to the city of Jerusalem, fem. sing.
“Wind.” Heb., ruʹach; Gr., aʹne·mon; Lat., venʹtum. That is, every direction to which the wind blows.

“And you will have to know that I am Jehovah.” Heb., wi·dhaʽ·temʹ ki-ʼaniʹ Yehwahʹ. The first of more than 60 occurrences of this phrase in Ezekiel, referring to the vindication of Jehovah’s name on earth.
“You,” fem. sing., referring to the “soil of Israel.”
Or, “The turn [of events].” The meaning and application of the Heb. word are uncertain.
Or, “I, Jehovah, am doing the striking.”
Or, “lamentation; wailing.” The meaning of the Heb. word is uncertain.
That is, from urination due to pressure from fear.
“It,” masc. sing., possibly referring to the precious metal.
“It,” fem. sing., likely referring to the holy city.
“The people of the land.” Heb., ʽam-ha·ʼaʹrets. Later used in a contemptuous sense. Compare Joh 7:47-49.
“A spirit.” Heb., ruʹach; Gr., pneuʹma; Lat., spiʹri·tus. Compare Ge 1:2 ftn, “Force.”

“The gate of the altar there was this symbol [Heb., seʹmel, “image”],” M; by substitution of a similar letter in M in harmony with LXXSy, “the gate toward the sunrising . . .”; by a slight change in vowel pointing in M, “the gate, there was the altar of this symbol.”
“This . . . jealousy.” Heb., haq·qin·ʼahʹ haz·zehʹ. See Ex 34:14 ftns.
“With Jaazaniah.” Heb., weYa·ʼazan·yaʹhu, meaning “Jehovah Gives Ear.”
Or, “There is no Jehovah seeing us.”
“The [god] Tammuz.” Heb., hat·Tam·muzʹ; Gr., ton Tham·mouzʹ; Lat., A·doʹni·dem.
Or, “the branch (twig).” Heb., haz·zemoh·rahʹ; doubtless used in idolatrous worship. It may represent the human male organ.
“My nose,” in the original Heb. text; M, “their nose.” One of the Eighteen Emendations of the Sopherim to avoid an apparent derogatory reference to Jehovah. See App 2B.
“And there was one man.” Heb., weʼish-ʼe·chadhʹ.
Lit., “the cherub.” Heb., hak·keruvʹ, sing. but likely in a collective sense. This is the first occurrence of the word in Eze. See 1:22-28.
Lit., “you must mark a mark.” The Heb. word for the noun “mark” is taw, the last letter of the Heb. alphabet, which was anciently a cross mark (×). See Job 31:35 where taw is translated “signature.”
“With the old men.” Heb., ba·ʼana·shimʹ haz·zeqe·nimʹ.
Or, “deeds of blood.” Lit., “bloods.” Heb., da·mimʹ.
Or, “and there is no Jehovah seeing.” See 8:12 ftn, “Seeing us.”
“God Almighty.” Heb., ʼEl-Shad·daiʹ; Gr., The·ouʹ Sad·da·iʹ; Lat., Deʹi O·mni·po·tenʹtis.
Meaning “Jehovah Has Provided Escape.” Heb., Pelat·yaʹhu.
“The men.” Heb., ha·ʼana·shimʹ, pl. of ʼish.
“She,” fem., referring to the “city” of Jerusalem.
Or, “active force.” Heb., ruʹach; Gr., pneuʹma; Lat., spiʹri·tus. See Ge 1:2 ftn, “Force.”
Lit., “and the ascents of your spirit.” Heb., u·ma·ʽalohthʹ ru·chakhemʹ.
Or, “it,” fem., referring to the “city” of Jerusalem.
“There will be a bringing forth.” In Heb. this is understood to be a verb in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time and impersonal, and used as the subject of the sentence.
“Them,” TLXXSyVg and many Heb. mss; M, “you,” pl.
Lit., “And into the heart.” Heb., weʼel-levʹ.
Or, “by the active force.” Heb., beruʹach; Gr., pneuʹma·ti; Lat., spiʹri·tu. See Ge 1:2 ftn, “Force”; Ge 6:17 ftn, “Active.”
“Wind.” Heb., ruʹach; Gr., aʹne·mon; Lat., venʹtum.
Or, “concerning the soil.” Heb., ʼel-ʼadh·mathʹ; TLXXVg, “upon the land.”
“Their own spirit.” Heb., ru·chamʹ; Lat., spiʹri·tum; Gr., kar·diʹas, “heart.”
According to M; LXX, “and I shall give hurling-stones against their bondings, and they will fall”; Vg, “and I shall give very large stones rushing from above.”
“And a blast of.” Heb., weruʹach; Gr., pneuʹma; Lat., venʹtum, “wind.”
Or, “it,” fem. sing.; not referring to the “wall,” masc., but possibly to the city.
“Souls.” Heb., nepha·shohthʹ, fem. pl.; Gr., psy·khasʹ; Lat., aʹni·mas.
“Souls.” Heb., nepha·shimʹ, masc., pl. of neʹphesh, fem. The only occurrence in M; hence, probably meant to read, choph·shimʹ, “free ones.”
“Any man at all.” Heb., ʼish ʼish.
Lit., “to them for God.” Heb., la·hemʹ lEʼ·lo·himʹ.
Lit., “the men.” Heb., ha·ʼana·shimʹ, pl. of ʼish.
The meaning of this Heb. expression is uncertain. LXX, “and you will by no means go in, nor will it by any means happen”; Vg, “just as it has not happened, neither is about to be.”
Or, “and commit unfaithful intercourse with them.” Heb., wat·tiz·ni-vamʹ; Lat., et for·ni·caʹta es in eʹis.
“My sons,” MSyVg; LXX and eight Heb. mss, “your sons.”
Or, “a torus,” on the foot of an altar, evidently for immoral purposes.
Possibly, “O how weak your heart is!”
Or, “that commits marital sexual unfaithfulness.” Heb., ham·mena·ʼaʹpheth; Gr., he moi·kho·meʹne; Lat., a·dulʹte·ra. See Mt 5:32 ftn, “Adultery.”
“They,” fem., referring to “Sodom” and her “dependent towns [lit., daughters].”
“Syria (Aram),” MTLXXVg; Sy and many Heb. mss and printed ed., “Edom.”
“It,” M, fem. sing., referring to the “kingdom”; margin of one Heb. ms, “him,” masc. sing., referring to the king.
“To every wind,” representing direction. Heb., lekhol-ruʹach; Gr., eis panʹta aʹne·mon; Lat., in oʹmnem venʹtum. Compare Ge 1:2 ftn, “Force.”
“The souls.” Heb., han·nepha·shohthʹ; Gr., psy·khaiʹ; Lat., aʹni·mae. See App 4A.
Or, “The soul that is sinning is the one that will die.” Heb., han·neʹphesh ha·cho·teʼthʹ hiʼ tha·muthʹ.
Lit., “done the brother of one of these things,” M; T, “done to his brother one of these things”; SyVg, “done (any) one of these things.”
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
Or, “thorns”; put through the cheek or nose of animals as well as of captives in order to lead them on a rope.
“Dwelling towers; palaces,” by the substitution of a letter; M, “widows.”
Possibly, “camp,” by changing the letter Taw to Chehth.
“In your blood,” MSyVg; two Heb. mss, “of your vineyard”; T, “she used to resemble.”
“Who is sanctifying them (holding them sacred; treating them as holy).” Heb., meqad·deshamʹ; Gr., ha·gi·aʹzon; Lat., sanc·tiʹfi·cans.
Or, “I, Jehovah, am your God.” Heb., ʼaniʹ Yehwahʹ ʼElo·heh·khemʹ.
“The southern quarter.” Heb., teh·maʹnah; Gr., thai·manʹ, a Gr. transliteration of the Heb. word; Lat., auʹstri.
“South.” Heb., da·rohmʹ; Gr., da·romʹ, a Gr. transliteration of the Heb. word; Lat., aʹfri·cum.
That is, from urination due to pressure from fear.
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
Lit., “It,” masc., referring to the “scepter,” masc.; not the “sword,” fem.
“Show yourself sharp,” fem., addressed to the “sword.”
“Should be cut out.” In Heb. this is a verb in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time and impersonal.
Or, “war cry,” by a transposition of letters.
“You,” fem. sing., evidently referring to Rabbah of the Ammonites.
Lit., “men of slander.” Heb., ʼan·shehʹ ra·khilʹ.
Lit., “your blood,” sing. but the subject of a pl. verb.
“Your uncleanness.” Heb., tum·ʼa·thekhʹ; Gr., a·ka·thar·siʹa. See 2Co 12:21 and Ga 5:19 ftns, “Uncleanness.”
“Blow,” by a correction; M, “deposit,” without an object.
Or, “it,” fem., referring to the city of Jerusalem.
“Souls.” Heb., nepha·shohthʹ; Lat., aʹni·mas. See App 4A.
Or, “a reputation.” Lit., “a name,” in a bad, infamous sense.
Lit., “more than the fornications.” Heb., miz·zenu·nehʹ; Gr., hy·perʹ ten por·neiʹan; Lat., suʹper for·ni·ca·ti·oʹnem. See App 5A.

Or, “shield-bearers.” Lit., “third men.” Heb., sha·li·shimʹ; Gr., tris·seʹ, “threefold”; Lat., duʹcum, “leaders.” Assyrian bas-reliefs show one of the three chariot occupants to be an armor-bearer or umbrella-bearer, a third man.
“Through the squeezing,” by a slight correction.
Possibly, “a multitude.” The meaning is uncertain.
“There will be a doing.” In Heb. this is a verb in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time and impersonal.
“To the men.” Heb., la·ʼana·shimʹ, pl. of ʼish.
“There will be the bringing up . . . a making.” In Heb. these are verbs in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time and impersonal.
“Empty out the broth,” by a correction; M, “let there be a spicing with the scented herbs.”
“Your,” fem. sing., addressed to the city.
“You,” fem. sing., referring to the country of Ammon.
“In [the] soul.” Heb., beneʹphesh; Gr., psy·khesʹ; Lat., aʹni·mo. See App 4A.
Or, “leaves of a door,” M; T, “tradeswoman.”
“Will go down,” MVg; TLXXSy, “he will bring down.”
According to M; Sy, “O inhabitress of the seas”; Vg, “you who dwell in the sea.”
Or, “surging waters.” Heb., tehohmʹ; LXXVg, “abyss.” Compare Ge 1:2 ftn, “Deep.”
“In cypress wood,” in agreement with T; M, “the daughter of the Ashurites.”
“And valorous men.” Heb., wegham·ma·dhimʹ; Lat., Pig·meʹi, “pygmies.”
Lit., “they (people) gave your articles of exchange.”
“Edom,” Sy and about 25 Heb. mss; M, “Aram”; Vg, “The Syrian.”
“And special foodstuff.” Heb., u·phan·naghʹ. The meaning is uncertain, but it is thought to be a kind of food.
“You have been broken,” LXXSyVg and three Heb. mss, the verb having the fem. gender termination.
“A god (divine one).” Heb., ʼel; Gr., the·osʹ; Lat., deʹus.
Or, “a human.” Heb., ʼa·dhamʹ; Gr., anʹthro·pos; Lat., hoʹmo.
“Garden.” Heb., gan; Gr., pa·ra·deiʹsou; Syr., par·dai·seh; Lat., pa·ra·diʹsi.
“God.” Heb., ʼElo·himʹ; Gr., The·ouʹ; Lat., Deʹi.
“You are the,” MTVg; by a different vowel pointing, “With the,” in agreement with LXXSy and Arabic.
Lit., “cherub of an anointing [possibly, expansion].” Heb., keruvʹ mim·shachʹ.

“You are the anointed king in the kingdom, and I have given you greatness,” T; LXX, “With the cherub I set you”; Sy, “You happened to be with the anointed cherub that is covering, and I set you”; Vg, “You are the cherub stretched out and protecting, and I set you.”
“They filled the midst of you,” M; Sy, “you filled your own midst”; T, “your storehouses were filled”; LXX, “you filled your storehouses”; Vg, “your inner parts were filled.”
“God.” Heb., ʼElo·himʹ; Gr., The·ouʹ; Lat., Deʹi.
“I shall destroy you, O cherub that is covering,” MSy; Vg, “I have destroyed you, O protecting cherub”; LXX, “the cherub led you away.”
“You have profaned,” MSyVg; LXXB, “I have profaned.”
Or, “I, Jehovah, am their God.” Heb., ʼaniʹ Yehwahʹ ʼElo·heh·hemʹ.
Or, “thorns”; put through the cheek or nose of animals as well as of captives in order to lead them on a rope.
“The hand,” MmarginVg and many Heb. mss; M, “your hand”; LXXSy, “their hand.”
“In the ships,” M; Lat., in tri·eʹri·bus, “in triremes”; LXXSy, “hastening.”
“An Assyrian,” MTLXXSyVg; by a correction, “I differentiate you as”; by a different correction, “A cypress.”
Or, “surging waters.” Heb., tehohmʹ; LXXVg, “the abyss.” See Ge 1:2 ftn, “Deep.”
“In its watercourses,” by a correction; M, “by its sending forth.”
“In the garden of God.” Heb., beghan-ʼElo·himʹ; LXXSyVg, “in the paradise of God.” Compare vs 9.
Or, “pleasantness,” in agreement with LXXVg. Compare Ge 2:8 ftn, “Eden.”
Or, “to the grave.” Heb., sheʼohʹlah; Gr., haiʹdou; Lat., in·ferʹnum. See App 4B.
“Seed,” by a correction in agreement with LXXSy; MVg, “arm.”
Possibly, “during your snortings”; or, “through your nostrils,” by a slight correction.
“Body of captives,” LXX; MSy, “breakdown [or, broken parts].”
LXX adds, “in the first month”; MTSyVg omit.
“He has,” by a slight correction in agreement with “his”; MLXXSyVg, “I have.”
“The people of the land.” Heb., ʽam-ha·ʼaʹrets. Later used as an expression of contempt. Compare Joh 7:47-49.
Or, “and the people of the land actually take a man [Heb., ʼish], one from their borders.”
Or, “as their lookout.” Heb., la·hemʹ letso·phehʹ.
Or, “his own life.” Heb., naph·shohʹ; Gr., psy·khenʹ; Lat., aʹni·mam. See App 4A.
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
“You,” masc. pl., TSy and 18 Heb. mss; M, “You,” fem. pl.
Lit., “between a sheep for the sheep.” Heb., behn-sehʹ la·sehʹ.
Lit., “to them for God.” Heb., la·hemʹ lEʼ·lo·himʹ.
Lit., “the time of the error of [the] end.”
Or, “Since blood you did not hate, blood itself also will.”
Or, “you people maintain a big mouth against me.”
Or, “earthling men.” Heb., ʼa·dhamʹ; Lat., hoʹmi·nes.
Lit., “one,” fem., referring to the land, fem.
“Bereave of children,” MmarginLXXSy and many Heb. mss; M, “cause to stumble.”
“They,” TLXXSyVg and some Heb. mss; M, “he,” or, “it.”
Or, “And I shall certainly hold sacred (treat as holy).” Heb., weqid·dash·tiʹ; Gr., ha·gi·aʹso; Lat., sanc·ti·fi·caʹbo.
Lit., “to you for God.” Heb., la·khemʹ lEʼ·lo·himʹ.
“Like the garden.” Heb., keghanʹ; Syr., par·dai·saʼ, “the paradise.”
“In the spirit of.” Heb., veruʹach. See Ge 1:2 ftn, “Force.”
“The wind.” Heb., ha·ruʹach. See Ge 1:2 ftn, “Force.”
Lit., “to them for God.” Heb., la·hemʹ lEʼ·lo·himʹ.
Or, “nasi.” Heb., na·siʼʹ; Gr., arʹkhon; Lat., prinʹceps.

“Gog [of] the land of Magog,” MT; LXX, “Gog and the land of Magog”; Sy, “Gog and against the land of Magog”; Vg, “Gog, the land of Magog.” “Magog” is an artificial form equivalent to “home of Gog,” according to KB, p. 493.
“Head chieftain.” Or, “chieftain of Rosh.” Vg, “head prince”; LXX, “ruler of Rosh”; Sy, “leader and head.”
Or, “you chieftain of Rosh, Meshech.” Vg, “head prince of Meshech”; T, “the head, great one of Meshech”; LXX, “ruler of Rosh, Meshech”; Sy, “leader and head of Meshech.”
Or, “that I, Jehovah, am holy in Israel.” Heb., ki-ʼaniʹ Yehwahʹ qa·dhohshʹ beYis·ra·ʼelʹ.
“And . . . men.” Heb., weʼan·shehʹ, pl. form of ʼish.
“With those passing through,” MT; LXXSy omit.
Meaning “Crowd.” Heb., Hamoh·nahʹ, the fem. form of Ha·mohnʹ in vss 11, 15.
Or, “horsemen,” in agreement with LXXSyVg; M, “war chariot.”
Or, “I will also hold myself sacred (treat myself as holy).” Heb., weniq·dashʹti; Gr., ha·gi·a·stheʹso·mai; Lat., sanc·ti·fi·caʹtus.
“In the visions of God.” Heb., bemar·ʼohthʹ ʼElo·himʹ.
“Man.” Heb., ʼish; Gr., a·nerʹ; Lat., vir.
“Son of man.” Heb., ben-ʼa·dhamʹ; Gr., hui·eʹ an·throʹpou; Lat., fiʹli hoʹmi·nis.
“The measuring reed.” Heb., qenehʹ ham·mid·dahʹ; Gr., kaʹla·mos; Lat., caʹla·mus men·suʹrae. Compare Ga 6:16 ftn, “Conduct”; Re 11:1.

“A cubit and a handbreadth.” A cubit of 44.5 cm (17.5 in.) and a handbreadth of 7.4 cm (2.9 in.) equaled about 51.8 cm (20.4 in.) and represented the long cubit. Hence, a “measuring reed of six cubits” equaled 3.11 m (10.2 ft).
“The thing built.” Heb., hab·bin·yanʹ; LXX, “outer (advance) wall.”
“And the open part of the porch of the gate on the outside was twenty cubits, the chambers of the gate being round about,” LXXB.
Vs 30, not found in LXXIt and some Heb. mss, is considered a dittography of vs 29.
The exact location of these four tables at the north gate is not stated.
“The gift offering.” Heb., haq·qor·vanʹ; Lat., ob·la·ti·oʹnis. See Mr 7:11.
“And upon ten steps they would go up to it,” LXX; Vg, “And by eight steps there would be an ascent to it.”
“The temple.” Heb., ha·heh·khalʹ; Gr., na·onʹ; Lat., temʹplum. See Mt 23:16 ftn.
Lit., “This is the Holy of the Holies.” Heb., zeh Qoʹdhesh haq·Qodha·shimʹ.
“Upward and upward.” Or, “from story to story,” according to a correction suggested in KB3, p. 580.
Lit., “the sea,” that is, the Mediterranean Sea. Heb., hai·yamʹ.

“The temple.” Heb., ha·heh·khalʹ. In M this word is marked with extraordinary points by the Sopherim, evidently to indicate that it was included here by mistake because the next sentence begins with the same word. See App 2A.
LXX adds: “and the width was two cubits.”
Lit., “To the temple.” Heb., la·heh·khalʹ; Gr., na·oiʹ; Lat., temʹplo. See vs 1 ftn, “Temple.”
Lit., “and to the holy place (sanctuary).” Heb., welaq·qoʹdhesh; Gr., ha·giʹoi; Lat., sanc·tu·aʹri·o.
“The outer courtyard,” MTLXXSyVg; LXXBagster, “the inner courtyard.”
“A way of one cubit,” MTVg; LXXSy, “the length was a hundred cubits.” See 40:5 ftn, “Handbreadth.”
Or, “the dining rooms of the sanctuary,” in agreement with LXX.
“From the holy place (sanctuary).” Heb., me·haq·qoʹdhesh; Gr., ha·giʹou.
“The western side.” Lit., “the wind of the sea,” that is, the Mediterranean Sea to the west.
“What is holy.” Or, “the sanctuary.” Heb., haq·qoʹdhesh; Lat., sanc·tu·aʹri·um.
“The glory of the God of Israel.” Heb., kevohdhʹ ʼElo·hehʹ Yis·ra·ʼelʹ.
“When I came,” M; ThVg and six Heb. mss, “when he came”; T, “when I prophesied for making [the city] waste away.”
“There were appearances,” M; LXX, “the vision of the chariot, that I saw (was).”
“A spirit.” Heb., ruʹach; Gr., pneuʹma; Lat., spiʹri·tus.
Or, “the glory of Jehovah filled the House.”
“This is,” T; LXX, “you have seen”; but M has only the particle that is the sign of the accusative case for the next word.
“At their death,” TTh and about 20 Heb. mss and ed.; M, “their high places”; LXX, “in the midst of them.”
“The sanctuary.” Heb., ham·miq·dashʹ; Gr., ha·giʹon; Lat., sanc·tu·aʹri·i.
“Rebelliousness,” M; T, “the rebellious people”; LXX, “the rebellious house.”
“A dead person.” Heb., meth; Gr., psy·khenʹ, “soul.”
Or, “earthling man.” Heb., ʼa·dhamʹ; Gr., an·throʹpou; Lat., hoʹmi·nem.
“The holy place.” Heb., haq·qoʹdhesh; Lat., sanc·tu·aʹri·um.
“There will not be, however, for them an inheritance,” Vgc.
“Upon your house,” MTVg; LXXSy, “upon your [pl.] houses.”
“The holy place.” Heb., haq·qoʹdhesh; Gr., ha·gi·aʹsma.
“And a sacred place.” Heb., u·miq·dashʹ; T, “a paved way.”
A liquid measure that equaled 22 L (5.81 gal) and corresponded to the ephah, a dry measure.
A homer equaled 220 L (200 dry qt).
An ephah equaled 22 L (20 dry qt).
A shekel weighed 11.4 g (0.367 oz t).
A gerah weighed 0.57 g (0.01835 oz t).
“Livestock,” by a correction of M; or possibly, to agree with LXX, “families”; M, “well irrigated [land].”
“The sanctuary.” Heb., ham·miq·dashʹ; Gr., haʹgi·on; Lat., sanc·tu·aʹri·um.
Or, “because of the individual.” Heb., me·ʼishʹ.
Lit., “as the gift of his hand.”
Lit., “what his hand may attain to (may reach).” See Le 5:7 ftn, “Afford.”
“He,” MmarginTLXXSyVg and over 100 Heb. mss; M, “they.”
Lit., “male lamb, a son of its year.” See Le 12:6; 14:10.
“You,” MT; LXXSyVg and some Heb. mss, “he.”
“You,” MT; LXXSyVg and two Heb. mss, “he.”
Or, “continual.” Heb., ta·midhʹ. Compare Da 8:11 ftn.
“On both rear sides,” Mmargin; M, “in the rear of them.”
“With corner structures.” Heb., mehuq·tsa·ʽohthʹ; LXXSyVg omit. In M this word is marked with extraordinary points by the Sopherim to stigmatize it as spurious and hence to be omitted. See App 2A.
“Had me return,” MTVg; Sy, “had me sit down”; LXX omits.
Or, “the desert plain.” See De 1:1 ftn, “Plains.”
“Into the sea, into the stinking waters, and the waters,” Sy.
“Living soul.” Heb., neʹphesh chai·yahʹ; Gr., psy·kheʹ ton zoiʹon; Lat., aʹni·ma viʹvens. See Ge 2:7 ftn, “Soul”; App 4A.
Lit., “two torrents,” M; TSy, “the waters of the torrent”; LXX, “the river”; Vg, “the torrent.”
Or, “will come to life; will live.” Heb., yich·yehʹ.
“In their kinds.” Heb., lemi·nahʹ; Lat., speʹci·es.

Lit., “its,” fem., referring to the “city,” fem.
“And the sanctuary of.” Heb., u·miq·dashʹ; Gr., ha·giʹa·sma; Lat., sanc·tu·aʹri·um.
